title: wt sweep --yes --json
description: What a wt sweep did, item by item. Printed by `wt sweep --yes --json [--expect <token>]` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the run. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

token.description: The token of the plan this run carried out; null when it stopped before one was made, or there was nothing to do.

outcome.description: done: every item to remove or delete went. refused: nothing was removed or deleted. partial: some went, some did not. interrupted: a signal ended the run.

error.description: Why the run stopped before touching anything: an --expect that no longer holds, the fetch, not the main checkout.

quarantine.description: Since 1.1.0. With --move-to <dir>: the folder, absolute. Each removed worktree went into a folder of its own in it, with its own recovery.json. null without it.

runId.description: Since 1.4.0. The run under refs/wt-swept/ the deleted branches were moved into, as wt refs sweep moves backups: wt refs swept lists it, wt refs restore puts them back, wt refs purge deletes them for good. null when no branch was moved: nothing was deleted, or only quarantined worktrees' branches, which the quarantine pins. A run a signal ended may name a run that holds only its meta.

category.description: Its part of the plan, as in the sweep-plan schema.

result.description: removed: the worktree and its branch are gone. deleted: the branch is gone. kept: left as it was, on purpose. failed: tried and not finished; worktreeRemoved and branchDeleted say what did happen. notRun: the run ended before it. interrupted: the one a signal caught.

reason.description: Why, for everything but removed and deleted.

pin.description: Since 1.4.0. The ref the deleted branch was moved into, refs/wt-swept/<runId>/heads/<branch>, read back holding tip; null when the branch was not moved there.

restoreCommand.description: When the branch was deleted: the argv that puts it back. Since 1.4.0 ["wt", "refs", "restore", runId, "--only", "refs/heads/<branch>", "--yes"] for a pinned branch, ["wt", "restore", <dir>] for a quarantined worktree's; the git branch form of 1.3.0 and before is no longer produced. null when the branch is there, or gone with no pin.

dir.description: This worktree's folder in the quarantine; wt restore <dir> puts it back.

adminMoved.description: Its admin dir is in <dir>/admin now: git no longer lists the worktree.

quarantine.description: Since 1.1.0. For a worktree the run moved, or tried to move, into the quarantine; null otherwise. Read from the folder after the row.

result.description: deregistered: the workspace was deleted, after the directory left its path and git stopped listing it. notRegistered: Superset is running and has no workspace there. skipped: the integration is off, Superset is not installed or not running, or the worktree was still there. failed: Superset erred. optedOut (since 1.3.0): --keep-superset; Superset was not asked.

superset.description: Since 1.2.0. For a worktree the run removed, what came of its Superset workspace; null when no worktree was removed. It changes neither result nor outcome.
